reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Scoring paraspinal tenderness as midline tenderness.
name: NEXUS Low-Risk Criteria (cervical spine)

version.label: NEXUS low-risk criteria (Hoffman et al. 2000)
version.detail: Five criteria; imaging was considered unnecessary only when all five were met. The criteria terms were deliberately left without strict definitions.

purpose: Identifies blunt trauma patients at low risk of cervical spine injury.
intendedPopulation: Patients with blunt trauma being considered for cervical spine imaging.

calculationMethod.share: NEXUS: {total == 0 ? 'all five low-risk criteria met' : (crit == 1 ? '1 criterion present' : crit + ' criteria present')}

resultStates.label: All five low-risk criteria met
resultStates.summary: No tenderness, deficit, altered alertness, intoxication or distracting injury.
resultStates.detail: In the derivation study imaging was considered unnecessary; clinical judgement still applies.

resultStates.label: Not all criteria met
resultStates.summary: One or more NEXUS criteria present: the rule's criteria for imaging are met.

clinicalContext.text: High sensitivity for clinically significant cervical spine injury in the derivation cohort.

clinicalInsights.text: The Canadian C-spine Rule had higher specificity in a head-to-head comparison; local protocols choose one.

limitations.text: Criteria terms are subjective (e.g. distracting injury), which reduces reliability.

limitations: Lower sensitivity reported in older adults in some studies.

guideSections.what: Five clinical criteria; when all are absent the patient is low risk for cervical spine injury.
guideSections.whenToUse: Blunt trauma patients considered for cervical spine imaging.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess each criterion; if any is present the rule's imaging criteria are met.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Supports, but does not replace, clinical judgement.

sources.citation: Hoffman JR, Mower WR, Wolfson AB, Todd KH, Zucker MI. Validity of a set of clinical criteria to rule out injury to the cervical spine in patients with blunt trauma. N Engl J Med. 2000;343(2):94-99.
